It could use an on/off switch. Extra heating element could use a stiff container to protect it. It functions as I expected from previous experiences. Using it to join surgical draping material ("Halyard 600") in some steps for making anti-viral face masks. It is fast to fuse the material, and very consistent in performance.

I am using thick 7 mil mylar bags for long term food packaging. It took multiple heat cycles (about 12) on the highest setting for the bags to securely seal, and I flipped the bags to seal on both sides, but that was not particularly a problem. The instructions (which were pretty poor) seem to indicate an "L" setting for long cycles, but the 16" unit I got only had 1-8 settings.  With a plastic bag, the seal is almost instant. Not super high quality manufacturing, but since there is not much to break, I expect this will last a long while.

I tried all the YouTube suggestions on fixing the ice maker in my Samsung fridge. Sometimes the ice-maker would work for one cycle but die again. I considered used units on Ebay but had to conclude they would probably die like mine since the defect was inherent in the original design. My wife had me making ice in trays. Old school. But she wouldn't fill them up. I'd want a cube and find the tray empty in the freezer. Girls!  I went with this new unit. It is an exact replacement. I'm hoping it has better components or at least lasts for years. I suggest looking up a YouTube video describing how to remove the door panel on the freezer. You need to unscrew it and lift it up and out to access the wire harness. It is easy but it helps to see someone do it. The videos are tied to the ice-maker model number and are usually in the title.  I'm happy to see the device working flawlessly. The familiar "avalanche sound" of ice dumping into the bin is satisfying. Haha. Don't put it off any longer.

My ice maker totally died.  The rest of the 9 year old fridge worked great.  So it was definitely worth taking a chance on replacing the ice maker.  I double check the replacement part number before ordering as there were two part numbers to choose from.  The part number is on a decal attached to the bottom of the ice maker.  I followed youtube video instruction to remove and replace the ice maker.  Removing the fridge panel was the hardest part as the pin connectors are very tight.  I had to pull pretty hard on the panel to free it.  Also the wiring harness removal requires the use of a screw driver to press down on the connector to release it.  The new ice maker is working great after a month's use.

The unit installed pretty easily after watching youTube video.  Be careful when working with cold plastic parts in the freezer door.  they break easily.  The unit is working great now that itis installed.
